Laws and regulations can require certain types of data to be stored, transmitted, and handled according to specific rules. § Personally identifiable information (PII) is any data that allows someone to be identified and includes (but is not limited to): name, signature, phone number, address, biometric data (e.g., fingerprints), social security number, date of birth, and email address. The protection of this data is covered by many laws but most notably The Privacy Act of 1974 and for children under the age of 13 the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998. § Protected health information (PHI) is any data related to an individual’s health, treatment, payment for healthcare at any time and includes (but is not limited to): test results, treatment records, hospital records, doctor visit notes, and health provider payment records. The protection of PHI is included in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996. § Payment card information (PCI) is the data collected by organizations to process payments via cards (e.g., credit cards) and includes the following: name, account number, expiration date, address, and CVV code. The protection of this data is regulated by the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS).
